The target needs no secret (registry entry in evaluation.json names no environmentKeys and launches app/server/grade.mjs locally), so the default is merge. CONTRIBUTING.md says merges go through the merge queue, which re-runs the test check on the queued commit, and .github/workflows/ci.yml lists merge_group, so the post-merge run exists. The preflight launches a local server with a 20000 ms ready timeout, well inside the 15-minute timeout of the ci.yml test job.

.github/workflows/nightly.yml runs on schedule (02:17 UTC) and workflow_dispatch and passes GRADER_MODEL_KEY. The contract declares a critical behavior (B-001) and docs/DEPLOYING.md says a grading defect reaches learners within 24 hours, so a nightly live run is justified. The nightly workflow is independent of the deploy, so this tier gates nothing and warns.
Held-out partition at the nightly event of .github/workflows/nightly.yml (schedule and workflow_dispatch), the default scheduled home. It runs the same nightly as the twin-run above.
Strength comparison against baseline/ at the nightly event of .github/workflows/nightly.yml; a regression is a warning by AD-10.

.github/workflows/deploy.yml ships main to production on its own schedule (03:47 UTC) and on workflow_dispatch, and those triggers are the release event. Its production job deploys with DEPLOY_TOKEN and has no needs, so it shares the file the CI skill edits and waits for this tier through gates. docs/DEPLOYING.md says a failed nightly run does not stop that night's deploy, so only this tier can stop a defective deploy.
